Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second chapter of this encounter! The umpires have stepped on the field. Ibrahim Zadran has a couple of words with his players in the huddle before the players take their fielding positions. Alishan Sharafu will be pairing with the skipper, Muhammad Waseem to open for the United Arab Emirates. Fareed Ahmad will operate with the new ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

As the United Arab Emirates prepare to embark on their run chase, the question lingers in the air - Can they successfully chase down the target, or will the Pathans' bowling unit rise to the challenge? The stage is set for a riveting second innings, where every run and wicket will shape the narrative of this encounter. Stay tuned as the second inning will start in no time.

Rahmanullah Gurbaz is in for a chat. He says that the wicket is not that easy and he was struggling a bit. He says that he will hopefully come back in form soon. Adds that he is excited for the final against Pakistan as they had beaten them in the last game. He says that they are well prepared for the finals and this game will help them with the preparation.

Post-drinks, the dynamics of the game shifted dramatically. The UAE bowlers, led by the impressive duo of Muhammad Farooq and Haider Ali, targeted the set batters with precision, turning the tide of the match. Simranjeet Singh seized the moment, claiming another vital wicket for his side and joining the fray with style. Though Karim Janat added a valuable 28 runs with his cameo, it was Haider Ali who rose to the occasion, quelling any potential threat with crucial wickets. Yet, just when it seemed the momentum had firmly shifted, Gulbadin Naib and Azmatullah Omarzai took charge, brilliantly dismantling the UAE's death bowling strategy. Their impressive performance in the closing overs, scoring 31 runs in the final three, reignited hope for the Pathans and set the stage for a thrilling finish.

Phew... what a rollercoaster of an inning! Despite the ups and downs, Afghanistan has set a competitive score of 170 runs on the board to challenge the UAE. However, reflecting on the first half of the innings, it's clear they had the potential to achieve even more.  Initially, at the start of the inning, the two openers for Afghanistan faced challenges in middling the deliveries. Yet, after a few overs, they found their rhythm, unleashing a barrage of boundaries that put the opposition bowlers firmly on the back foot. Their partnership blossomed into a formidable 98 runs off 72 balls. The Pathans were riding high, with everything falling into place, until the drinks break disrupted their momentum.
Short, on leg, Gulbadin Naib leaves it alone. He instantly regrets leaving the ball. That was quite strange from Gulbadin Naib. Afghanistan end their innings at 170/4!

Commentary.Commentary: The moment we've all been waiting for is finally here! We are ready for the play to kick off, and the electric atmosphere in Sharjah Cricket Stadium is truly undeniable. The umpires are out in the field and so are the players of United Arab Emirates. Rahmanullah Gurbaz will be pairing with Ibrahim Zadran to open the inning for Afghanistan. Junaid Siddique will get the job to start with the new ball. Here we go...

United Arab Emirates (Playing XI) - Muhammad Waseem (C), Alishan Sharafu, Muhammad Zohaib (In for Ethan D'souza), Asif Khan, Rahul Chopra (WK), Harshit Kaushik, Haider Ali, Muhammad Farooq (In for Muhammad Jawadullah), Muhammad Rohid, Junaid Siddique, Simranjeet Singh (In for Dhruv Parashar).

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran (C), Azmatullah Omarzai, Karim Janat, Sharafuddin Ashraf (In for Sediqullah Atal), Gulbadin Naib (In for Mohammad Nabi), Abdullah Ahmadzai (In for Rashid Khan), Mohammad Ishaq (In for Darwish Rasooli), Fareed Ahmad (In for Allah Mohammad), Noor Ahmad, Mujeeb Ur Rahman (In for Fazalhaq Farooqi).
TOSS - Afghanistan won the coin flip and have elected to BAT first.

This match is set to be an electrifying encounter! United Arab Emirates will be eager to pull off an upset, while Afghanistan aims to sustain their impressive winning streak. Fans can look forward to a thrilling contest between these two teams. Stay tuned for the toss and team news coming up shortly!

In a remarkable display of skill and strategy, Afghanistan has already clinched their place in the finals! In their latest match against Pakistan, they set a challenging target of 170 runs and then showcased their bowling prowess by restricting Pakistan to just 151 runs for 9 wickets. The victory was a collective effort, with Fazalhaq Farooqi, Rashid Khan, Mohammad Nabi, and Noor Ahmad all making significant contributions with the ball. Their remarkable performance not only secured the win but also demonstrated their readiness and determination to compete at the highest level!

In their recent encounter, UAE faced a formidable challenge against Pakistan, resulting in a hard-fought 31-run loss. Despite a stellar effort from Alishan Sharafu, who brilliantly scored 68 runs off just 51 balls, the team fell short in their pursuit of victory. The standout performer for Pakistan was undoubtedly Haider Ali, whose exceptional bowling figures of 2 for 17 were pivotal in stifling UAE's chase. This match showcased the determination and talent of UAE, but in the end, they couldn't quite seize the win.

Welcome to a high-spirited clash where pride is on the line. The United Arab Emirates will look to sign off on a high note in the T20I Tri-Series as they take on Afghanistan in their final league game. Despite being knocked out of contention for a place in the final, UAE will play for pride and aim to end their campaign with a win.
... MATCHDAY ...

After a week of intense action, the Tri-Series in the UAE reaches its final league clash as Afghanistan square off against United Arab Emirates at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium. Afghanistan took control in their first meeting with a convincing win, but the hosts will be determined to turn the tables this time and avoid a repeat outcome. Their defeat against Pakistan less than a day ago helped both Pakistan and Afghanistan to advance into the final of the tri-series. With nothing to lose, and a lot to prove, the United Arab Emirates will stride out taking the positives but more importantly, with an aim to correct the mistakes, which, in all fairness, have been recurring in nature. For instance, the top order provides solid starts through skipper Muhammad Waseem, but the middle order fails spectacularly to build stability in the middle overs. There have been flashes of brilliance from the likes of Alishan Sharafu, Asif Khan, and Rahul Chopra, but all have been fought lonely, with barely any support from the other end. Secondly, with the ball, they have been actually brilliant in controlling almost 80 percent of the innings, but it’s that crucial death-over phase where the Arabs have lacked control, by being a bit too predictable on tracks which can prove fruitful if variations are dished out. Afghanistan’s biggest strength has been their spin attack, with Rashid Khan leading the way. The wizard also happens to be the leading wicket-taker of the series. They have shuffled the personnel at times and every spinner has stepped up, whether it is Sharafuddin Ashraf, Noor Ahmad, or the experienced Mohammad Nabi. They have made the most of Sharjah’s slow and low surface. On the other hand their pace unit still has room for improvement with runs leaking at stages and a need for more control in the crucial patches. Batting-wise, different players have stepped up on different occasions, but the Afghans would desperately want their star opener, Rahmanullah Gurbaz to fire up the order. So far, he has the highest score of 38 this series, with consecutive single-digit scores, and he too, would like to ramp up his performance before the big final. The Afghans could also rest a few faces and throw an opportunity to the ones who didn’t get to feature in this series, trying to test the bench strength. In cricketing terms, it is a dead rubber, but with the Asia Cup just a few days away, both sides will be desperate to get the wrongs corrected. Chasing has been a tough gig in this entire series, with all five matches so far won by the teams batting first. Will that trend change this time around? Can the hosts UAE throw a tough challenge to the spirited Afghans? It is all set up for an exciting clash.
